summary: Live traffic surgical unwind for tenant prefetched KV + mixed-precision quant profile causing intermittent 5xxs
description:
Issue summary: Customer LumenDocs reports an increase in transient 5xx errors and request timeouts after a tenant-targeted optimizer profile rollout (mixed-precision quant + aggressive KV prefetch + higher batching). Impact: ~2% of requests for the tenant are returning 5xx (predominantly 524/timeout-from-backend and some 500s), observed spikes in tail latency and occasional memory pressure on serving pods. Environment: Dedicated pool (tenant LUMEN-88), prod us-east, pinned model redwood-xl-13b-v2-int8 rolled 2026-03-09 02:00 UTC with optimizer profile "hybrid-prefetch-q4-aggr"

Steps to reproduce:
1) Route LumenDocs test token through prod us-east endpoint with tenant header X-Tenant: LUMEN-88
2) Send mixed-length chat requests (some >1k tokens) and synthetic high-concurrency bursts (30rps sustained)
3) Observe increased 5xx rates, KV cache evictions, and OOM/kernel warnings in pod logs

Observed behavior: Intermittent 5xx and increased tail latency (95/99th), high KV cache miss churn, sporadic worker restarts on nodes serving the tenant pool. Expected behavior: Stable success rate and tail latency within SLO after optimizer rollout. Logs/metrics: Attached links to customer request IDs, Grafana panels show uptick in pod memory RSS, KV eviction rate, and request queue length behind the runtime. No code change to model was made by customer. Attachments: gzipped sample request logs, tenant rollout config JSON, Grafana screenshot links.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:15 - Maya Chen (Customer): Provided sample request IDs and flagged that issue started shortly after the optimizer profile toggle at 02:00 UTC.

2026-03-10 10:02 - Raj Patel (Support): Acknowledged and opened investigation. Requested permission to perform a non-disruptive traffic gate (10% shadow rollback) and to run a live telemetry capture for 15 minutes.

2026-03-10 11:20 - SRE Oncall (Priya Singh): Noted correlated node-level oom_killer events at ~02:30 UTC on node ip-10-0-23-9. Suggested checking kernel dmesg and cgroups mem_high events. Recommended lowering tenant batch size or disabling KV prefetch as quick mitigations.

2026-03-10 13:40 - Engineering (Diego Morales): Observed that the quant profile applies a memory-heavy fused-kernel path that increases per-worker RSS at higher sequence lengths. Suggested surgical unwind approach: disable KV prefetch first (lowest impact), drop async batching window second, and only then revert quant profile to lower-precision fallback if instability persists.
2026-03-11 07:05 - Maya Chen (Customer): Approved support to perform staged mitigations during low-traffic window and requested rollback checklist.

2026-03-11 12:00 - Raj Patel (Support): Executed staged mitigations per runbook: disabled KV prefetch at tenant level, observed immediate drop in eviction churn; retained batch settings. Continued monitoring.
2026-03-12 09:30 - Maya Chen (Customer): Reports 99th latency improved and 5xxs reduced to baseline. Requested confirmation of permanent settings and notes on follow-up actions.
2026-03-12 11:45 - Raj Patel (Support): Marked investigation as complete; documented rollback steps and follow-ups below. Will schedule a call to review long-term mitigations.
investigation_notes: Telemetry: Correlation between KV prefetch enablement and increase in memory RSS per worker for sequences > 1024 tokens.
Hypothesis: Combined memory footprint of prefetched KV + fused int8 kernel buffers causes transient memory pressure leading to worker restarts in tight concurrency bursts.
Checked artifacts: node dmesg, pod kubelet events, runtime heap profiles (heapster traces), batch size histograms, kv cache hit/miss timeseries.
Attempted non-invasive repro in staging with same optimizer profile reproduced increased RSS, confirming hypothesis.
Risk assessment: Immediate full revert of quant profile triggers throughput drop and potential cost increase; best to progressively unwind features with minimal customer impact.
workarounds: Disable tenant KV prefetch flag (applied 2026-03-11 12:00 UTC) — immediate reduction in KV eviction churn and tail latency.
Temporarily lower tenant max_batch_size from 32 to 16 via tenant config page to limit per-worker memory pressure.
If instability persists, fall back to the model's conservative quant profile (redwood-xl-13b-v2-int8 -> redwood-xl-13b-v2-q4-conservative) during a defined maintenance window.
Use traffic-split to route 20% of production to conservative profile first for validation before full rollback.
resolution: Applied staged surgical unwind: 1) Disabled KV prefetch for tenant LUMEN-88 (non-disruptive) on 2026-03-11 12:00 UTC. 2) Lowered tenant max_batch_size to 16 as a protective throttle. Observed immediate drop in 5xx and 99th latency within 45 minutes. Customer confirmed improvement on 2026-03-12. No rollback of quant profile performed to avoid performance regression; instead we recommended a controlled re-test with instrumented sampling and a temporary cap on sequence length. Follow-ups scheduled: roadmap item to add a tenant-level 'safemode' toggle that atomically disables KV prefetch + async batching and an integration test to catch combined memory-heavy optimizer profiles.
